clue.text: Perhaps the people who work for you–material workers, with stripes to show for it.

definitions.text: with stripes to show for it

parts.words: Perhaps the people who work for you
parts.note: your staff are the people employed by you; 'Perhaps' flags it as one example of such people
serge is a hard-wearing twilled cloth
ants are the stock crossword workers, from the worker ant

explanation.surface: An employer's workforce, pictured as cloth-makers who have earned their stripes.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer's two halves are clued in turn and then the whole is defined by the chevrons on the sleeve.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergeants of every kind wear stripes on the sleeve as badges of rank, so these senior NCOs have stripes to show.

clue.text: If a storm pans out this way on the boat, we expect it to be good with the athletic types.

definitions.text: we expect it to be good with the athletic types

indicators.note: on puts the vessel after the shuffled letters in this down answer
pans out describes the storm's letters working out into another order

explanation.surface: A storm at sea turns out fine and the crew prove good sports.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs on from 1 down into 21 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Sportsmanship is fair, gracious conduct, the standard of behaviour expected from athletes.

clue.text: Has enough money to pay for the little notices, very loud otherwise, inside.

definitions.text: Has enough money to pay for

indicators.note: inside places the following pieces within the short word for notices

parts.note: ads are advertisements, notices cut short
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Someone can pay for small notices, though not loud ones.
explanation.definitionFit: To afford something is to have sufficient means to buy it.

clue.text: The distance between the water and the deck–but the meals are provided gratis!

definitions.text: The distance between the water and the deck

parts.note: board means daily meals, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A ship's measurement, with a cheerful note that the food on board is free.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's second half is 'free board' spelt out in reverse order; 'but' merely joins it.
explanation.definitionFit: Freeboard is the nautical term for the height of a ship's side from the waterline to the main deck.

clue.text: Food of the east prepared here?

indicators.note: food is prepared by being worked over, so the letters of the compass word are reworked

explanation.surface: A question whether this is where oriental food is cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is a casual word for food or a meal.

clue.text: Showing unselfishness, crazy Yogi enters.

definitions.note: a verbal phrase used as a noun, the act of being unselfish

indicators.note: crazy suggests something disordered, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A mad yogi comes in and turns out to be selfless.
explanation.definitionFit: Generosity is liberality with one's time or money, the quality of putting others first.

clue.text: Everybody covered, but awful tired!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: everyone included, all inside
second meaning: exhausted, an informal phrase

explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' is the American colloquial intensifier, meaning very.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means everyone included, as in a total price, and also utterly exhausted.

clue.text: Packing by light strokes, and recording things around the morning.

indicators.note: around places the recording word on both sides of the letter for morning

parts.note: M is a dictionary abbreviation for morning, as in the Latin meridies of a.m.

explanation.surface: Someone packs things down gently while recording in the early hours.
explanation.definitionFit: To tamp is to press material down firmly with repeated light blows, as when filling a pipe or a blasthole.

clue.text: Thinking rather dreamily of a collection of yarns.

parts.note: a gathering is a collection of things or people

explanation.surface: Musing idly over a heap of knitting yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs on from 8 down into 16 down. 'Yarns' looks like tales, but here it means knitting wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolgathering is indulging in aimless daydreams, an idiom from wandering after scraps of fleece.

clue.text: The cop when not on duty still shows up the pre-hippie type.

definitions.text: The cop when not on duty still shows up the pre-hippie type.

parts.words: The cop when not on duty
parts.note: a policeman off duty is literally off his beat, the round he patrols
the Beats, or beatniks, were the 1950s bohemians before the hippies; their name is still visible at the end of the answer

explanation.surface: An off-duty policeman reveals himself to be a throwback bohemian.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, a patrolman away from his round is 'off beat'; the unconventional sense of the hyphenated word fits the Beat-generation bohemian, whose label sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Offbeat means unconventional or eccentric, exactly the reputation of the beatniks who came before the hippies.

clue.text: Will eating it make you indolent and self-indulgent? It makes Leo numb.

definitions.text: Will eating it make you indolent and self-indulgent?

indicators.note: the clue says it makes Leo numb, so the letters of those two words are made into the answer by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A question about a drowsy diet, then a remark that it sedates a lion.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Odyssey the lotus-eaters lost all will to go home; this is the botanical genus of the lotus, an obscure word the anagram makes fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelumbo is the genus of the sacred lotus, the plant whose eaters in Homer sank into dreamy, idle self-indulgence.

clue.text: Brewed broths–described by more than one end of 9.

definitions.text: described by more than one end of 9

indicators.note: a brew is stirred up and mixed, so the letters of the soup word are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Soups being brewed, then a cross-reference to another answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 across is OFFBEAT; its end is BEAT, and more than one of those is beats, which is what the answer means. The soups are only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Throbs are pulses or beats, so the plural of the last half of the other answer describes them.

clue.text: Quietly hurried, yet laid back for meals and such.

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase standing for an adjective

indicators.note: laid back means the word laid is read backwards here

explanation.surface: Someone rushed quietly yet stayed relaxed about mealtimes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid back' reads as relaxed, but it tells you to reverse 'laid'. P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: Prandial is the formal adjective for anything to do with a meal, as in post-prandial drowsiness.

clue.text: Right from the horse's mouth, an article buried deep.

parts.note: low down means deep beneath the surface

explanation.surface: A tip from an insider, and an item buried far below ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowdown is the inside information, and news straight from the horse's mouth comes from the most direct source.

clue.text: Cuts the lass–she is disturbed by it!

indicators.note: disturbed things are thrown out of order, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone cuts a girl, who is upset by it.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl and the pronoun together give exactly the seven letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Slashes are long sweeping cuts, and as a verb slashes means cuts with a blade.

clue.text: The short periodical is about to go–like one of the survivors of a race of giants.

definitions.text: one of the survivors of a race of giants

parts.note: a mag is a magazine cut short

indicators.note: about signals turning the word go round so it is read backwards

explanation.surface: A news item about a magazine folding, compared to the last of a race of giants.
explanation.walkthrough: In British legend Gog and Magog were the last of the giants of Albion, captured by Brutus and set to guard London.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend makes the pair the last two giants left alive in ancient Britain, so the answer is one of those survivors.

clue.text: What the revenuers sought at one time, but only at night?

definitions.text: What the revenuers sought at one time
definitions.meaning: first meaning: illicit whiskey, hunted by tax agents
second meaning: light from the moon, seen only after dark

explanation.walkthrough: Revenuers were US federal tax agents who raided illegal stills during and after Prohibition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means illegally distilled liquor and, literally, the light of the moon.

clue.text: See 8
Famous–but not little Edward.

parts.note: Ed is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Someone is well known, though not the boy called Eddie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But not' looks like an exclusion, yet the word not is used as it stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means well known or celebrated, a close synonym of famous.

clue.text: Hobo with the Paris-style put under-foot.

explanation.surface: A vagrant in French fashion gets trodden on.
explanation.definitionFit: To trample is to tread heavily on something, crushing it under the feet.

clue.text: What the plump lady perhaps does to the dress, or the man to the cat.

definitions.text: What the plump lady perhaps does to the dress
definitions.meaning: first meaning: enlarges a garment by releasing the seams
second meaning: lets the animal go outdoors

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning borrows the verb from the first half: what the man does to the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both making clothes wider at the seams and releasing a pet out of the house.

clue.text: A place where you get to stumble on oil production?

indicators.note: production suggests something worked up out of raw material, so the letters of the fuel are reworked

explanation.surface: A spot where you might fall over during oil drilling.
explanation.walkthrough: The Libyan capital fits the surface, as the country is an oil producer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is a city, the capital of Libya, so it is a place on the map.

clue.text: They supposedly homeward fly, but a person sometimes does to his pride.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: migrating birds famous for returning home each spring

definitions.text: a person sometimes does to his pride
definitions.meaning: second meaning: to swallow one's pride is to set it aside

explanation.walkthrough: The plural noun and the third-person verb are spelt alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The migratory birds return each year to the same nests, and the idiom about pride uses the verb for gulping something down.

clue.text: See 1
The little girl in kilts has nothing to catch cows with!

parts.note: lass is the Scottish word for a girl, hence the kilts

explanation.surface: A Scottish girl has no way to catch cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a looped rope a cowboy throws to catch cattle; the definition is a phrase standing for the noun.

clue.text: Is this what makes an angry snake bite? One might hope so.

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake, Cleopatra's
ire is anger; the adjective stands for the noun, as an angry snake is a snake with ire

explanation.surface: A wry question about whether an angry snake bites, answered with hopeful sarcasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An angry snake' is to be read as the snake followed by the anger, in that order.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to hope or long for something ambitious.

clue.text: Atlantic hideout for one in opposition.

indicators.note: a hideout is where something is hidden, so the answer is concealed inside the ocean's name

parts.note: the ocean's name holds the four letters in its middle, between the opening Atl and closing c

explanation.surface: A refuge on the Atlantic for a dissident.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti is a person who is against something, an opponent.

clue.text: One sees part of him past operating a paintbrush to achieve it.

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is seen, so the answer lies hidden within them

parts.note: the run of letters begins at the end of him and finishes on the first letter of operating

explanation.surface: A glimpse of a man at work with a paintbrush.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: it is a painting technique that needs a brush or knife to achieve.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is paint laid on thickly so that the brush or knife strokes stand up from the canvas.

clue.text: Frantic, a robin gets one in the capital.

indicators.note: a frantic thing is wildly agitated, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A frantic robin finds one of its kind in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya.

clue.text: Casing the landscape–again, fool? No, I remove "h" from the circle.

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to con is to fool or trick

indicators.note: remove tells you to take the named letter out of the following words

explanation.surface: A puzzled reconnaissance: being fooled again, and a letter dropped from a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: The spelling is the American one, with -ER-, as befits a New York magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconnoitre is to survey ground before an operation, and casing a place means scouting it out beforehand.
